goal: Barkdown runs its library without a source checkout or an Elixir toolchain on the machine: the runtime is a packaged release, and step by step the rest of what an installation needs.
scope: A profile's runtime from a packaged Barkpark release, built and stamped by a script
The portable profile, crash reclaim and recovery unchanged on the packaged runtime
The app itself as a macOS application that carries its runtime
acceptance: With only system folders on the PATH the app boots a profile's runtime, writes, restarts and reads the same
Export, import and reclaim after a kill pass on the packaged runtime
A machine with no Postgres installed runs a profile
A built macOS application starts a profile with nothing else installed
nextAction: 1) Licences of everything the application carries (Erlang/OTP, the server's Elixir packages, Postgres, OpenSSL) collected into the third-party notices; nothing is handed to another person before that. 2) A Mac without developer tools runs the application: a clean account on this Mac, and a signature other than ad hoc. 3) Size: the two agent command-line tools are half of the 1 GB. 4) The provider truth runner's successful-edit scenarios on a Paper under the isolated runtime (left by C087).
truthReview: 2026-09-30: the macOS application is built with the runtime folder inside and started as an application, with only system folders on the PATH: a never-configured profile runs on the carried server and Postgres, New page makes a Paper, and the note reads the same after a restart. Built and run on one Mac, signed ad hoc, not notarized, started from its build folder with --profiles. The runtime folder rehearsal covers export, import and reclaim. No Mac without developer tools has run either. Windows is not covered. Resumed 2026-10-01 after C087 closed.
screenshotReview: No renderer change. Live screenshots of a note on the packaged runtime and in the built application are in the rehearsal folders.
